E01.definition: Settled by the gateway inside the period and credited by the bank after period end. The money exists and is identified; only the date is on the wrong side of the cut. Auto-clears next period without intervention.
E01.title: Timing / in-transit

E02.definition: The gateway charged a rate the commercial agreement does not support. The bank and settlement legs still tie, so this is invisible to a two-way match. It does NOT need the contract: a gateway bills its book on one set of terms, so rows on different terms disagree with their own peers, and the size of the disagreement is the finding. Which side of that disagreement is wrong needs a human — the majority is not automatically right. Books to fee variance so it never disappears into the ordinary fee line.
E02.title: Fee variance vs contract

E03.definition: A residual attributable to currency conversion or sub-unit rounding, within the tolerance policy states. Above the policy threshold it is not this code — an unexplained residual must never be absorbed as rounding.
E03.title: FX or rounding difference

E04.definition: The counterparty paid part of what was invoiced. The remainder is still owed, so the receivable stays open; this is not a write-off and must not be closed as one.
E04.title: Partial payment

E05.definition: More money arrived than was invoiced. The surplus is a liability to the payer until it is applied or refunded, so it is held rather than recognised.
E05.title: Overpayment / on-account

E06.definition: The same economic event appears twice in a source, typically an export defect rather than a second payment. Never auto-suppressed: two genuinely identical transactions exist, so a distinguishing field is required before either is dropped.
E06.title: Duplicate

E07.definition: A reversal landed against a transaction from a period that is already closed. Books to the dispute reserve rather than reopening a closed period.
E07.title: Chargeback after period close

E08.definition: Cash arrived in the bank with no settlement advice behind it. The balance must reflect the money; what it is for is unknown, so it is held in unapplied cash rather than guessed into revenue.
E08.title: Missing remittance

E09.definition: Two or more distinct subsets of settlement rows sum to the same payout within tolerance. There is no correct answer to pick, so the alternatives travel with the exception and a human chooses. An honesty code: no answer beats a confident wrong one.
E09.title: Netting ambiguity

E10.definition: The payout reference was truncated, transposed or stripped in transit, so the match key no longer resolves. The money and the amount are intact; the identifier is not.
E10.title: Reference corruption

E11.definition: The same counterparty appears under two names across sources — a rename, a legal-entity change, or a formatting difference. A master-data fix, not a cash finding.
E11.title: Counterparty alias

E12.definition: The transaction belongs to a different legal entity or ledger than the one being reconciled. Posting it here would be correct arithmetic in the wrong books.
E12.title: Wrong entity

E13.definition: The subset-sum search hit a stated compute bound before proving uniqueness. This is a finding about our capacity, never about the data, and reporting it as ambiguity would let a capacity limit masquerade as a business fact. An honesty code.
E13.title: Solver timeout

E14.definition: No strategy produced a match and the engine cannot say why. It carries the facts it has — amount, row count, best residual — and leaves classification to triage. An honesty code: 'I do not know' said out loud beats a plausible guess that routes work to the wrong desk.
E14.title: Unexplained
